title: Iran Air 291
summary: Iran Air Flight 291 crashed into the Alborz Mountains 29 kilometers north of Tehran during approach. The crew received navigation instructions that placed them 17 miles off course to the north. When the First Officer warned that the VORTAC was giving incorrect information, the captain did not respond.
probable_cause: Navigation error placing aircraft 17 miles north of intended course; poor cockpit communication when First Officer warned of navigation discrepancy; inoperable ILS and ground radar.

factors.evidence: foggy and snowy weather conditions
Without receiving instructions from the controller, the pilots were 17 mi off course to the north
the first officer told the captain that the VORTAC was giving the wrong radial course, but he did not respond
The aircraft collided with the Alborz Mountains, 29 km north of Tehran

events.text: Flight 291 departed from Mashad Airport bound for Tehran-Mehrabad Airport.
The controller at Mehrabad airport in Tehran gave the crew a direct approach to runway 29.
The dispatcher instructed the crew to take a 360° heading to reach the non-directional beacon of the Varamin approach.
The first officer told the captain that the VORTAC was giving the wrong radial course.
Without receiving instructions from the controller, the pilots were 17 mi off course to the north.
The aircraft collided with the Alborz Mountains, 29 km north of Tehran.

title: LOT Polish Airlines 007
summary: LOT Polish Airlines Flight 007, an Ilyushin Il-62, was approaching Warsaw-Okęcie Airport on 14 March 1980 when the crew reported landing gear indicator issues and initiated a go-around. During the go-around, the low-pressure turbine of engine 2 disintegrated, ejecting fragments that damaged engines 1 and 3, severed control rods for rudder and elevator, and cut power cables for the flight data recorder and voice recorder. The aircraft entered an uncontrolled dive and crashed. All 87 people on board were killed.
probable_cause: Defects in materials and faults in the manufacturing process of the Kuznetsov NK-8 jet engine shaft, and weaknesses in the design of its turbine. Manufacturing defects created stress concentration, incorrect heat-treatment, and contaminant particles that accelerated fatigue fracture of the shaft.

factors.evidence: weaknesses in the design of its turbine
During manufacture, a sharp 90-degree step was made resulting in stress concentration; incorrectly heat-treated shaft with contaminant particles resulted in accelerated fatigue fracture
the low-pressure turbine of engine 2 disintegrated after nine seconds; one piece of turbine disc was ejected upwards
The third piece of the disc shot into the hull, severed the rudder and elevator control rods and destroyed engine 3
when the control rods were cut, the tail section's horizontal stabilizer dropped down, causing the nose to go down
aircraft impacted the ice-covered moat of a military fortress at a speed of approximately 380 km/h at a 20-degree down angle

events.text: The crew reported to ATC that the landing gear indicator light was not operating.
The crew decided to go around and allow the flight engineer to check if the landing gear issue was caused by a burnt fuse or actual gear problem.
When thrust was applied to all four engines, the low-pressure turbine of engine 2 disintegrated after nine seconds.
The third piece of the turbine disc shot into the hull and severed the rudder and elevator control rods and destroyed engine 3.
When the control rods were cut, the horizontal stabilizer dropped under its own weight, causing the aircraft nose to go down.
The aircraft impacted the ice-covered moat at a speed of approximately 380 km/h at a 20-degree down angle, 950 m from the runway threshold.

title: Transbrasil 303

location.name: Morro da Virgínia, Ratones, near Florianópolis

summary: Transbrasil Flight 303, a Boeing 727-27C on a night instrument approach to Hercílio Luz International Airport in Florianópolis during a severe thunderstorm, went off course around 20:38 and struck the hill Morro da Virgínia, killing 55 of 58 aboard. Lightning had disrupted the Florianópolis NDB -- the airport's only navigation aid -- producing a false position indication that left the crew, piloted by a trainee inspector under a supervising commander, overconfident of their location and unable to abort the approach before descending below the region's safety altitude.
probable_cause: Probable causes were misjudgment of speed and distance, inadequate flight supervision, failure to initiate a go-around, and improper operation of the engines.

factors.evidence: The aircraft was on a night instrument approach ... in a severe thunderstorm
unlike the major airports of the time using the VOR and ILS / DME systems, Florianópolis airport used the obsolete NDB as the only aid to navigation
the incidence of lightning hampered the operation of the NDB of Florianópolis, generating a false block of position, which impaired the judgment of the crew
The crew's overconfidence of their geographic position prevented the approach being done from being aborted
The aircraft was piloted by an inspector from the Civil Aviation Department, who was training for the Boeing 727's supervisory role ... inadequate flight supervision
failure to initiate a go-around
collided with Morro da Virgínia, hitting the trees until it reached the north side of the hill

events.text: After reaching Florianópolis' non-directional beacon near the Hercílio Luz bridge, the aircraft descended from 3,000 ft and began its landing approach during a severe thunderstorm.
Lightning hampered the operation of the Florianópolis NDB, generating a false indication of the aircraft's position that impaired the crew's judgment.
Overconfident of their geographic position, the crew continued the approach rather than initiating a go-around.
Around 20:38 the aircraft went off course, descended below the region's safety limit of about 60 m, and struck the north side of Morro da Virgínia.
The heavy impact with trees destroyed the fuselage, throwing passengers clear, including the few who survived.

title: Dan-Air 1008
summary: Dan-Air Flight 1008 was cleared to join a nonstandard unpublished holding pattern without a chart. Following ambiguous ATC instructions, the captain turned left toward terrain where the MSA was 14500 ft while cleared to descend to 5000 ft. The GPWS activated and the crew initiated a climb but the aircraft struck Mount La Esperanza while flying in cloud. The investigation found tardy and ambiguous ATC directions contributed to disorientation and the altitude clearance was inadequate for the terrain.
probable_cause: Crew flew aircraft into terrain at altitude insufficient for holding pattern in high-terrain area after receiving ambiguous ATC directions for an unpublished procedure.

factors.evidence: aircraft struck Mount La Esperanza at 13:21:15 local time
pilot in command, without taking account of the altitude at which he was flying, took the aircraft into an area of high terrain
tardy and ambiguous directions from air traffic control regarding the unpublished hold directly contributed to the disorientation of the aircraft commander
The aircraft was flying in cloud when it struck the mountain
directed altitude of 5000 ft was inadequate for this holding pattern

events.text: The aircraft was cleared to join a nonstandard holding pattern over the FP beacon without a chart.
The pilot turned the aircraft to the left towards the southeast into an area of high ground.
The ground proximity warning system activated as the aircraft descended toward high terrain.
The crew reacted quickly and initiated a climb with engines at full power.
The aircraft entered a steep turn to the right and struck Mount La Esperanza at 13:21:15 local time while flying in cloud.

title: Thai Airways 231
summary: Thai Airways Flight 231, a Hawker Siddeley HS 748, entered a severe thunderstorm during approach to Bangkok on 27 April 1980. A sudden downdraft at 1,500 feet caused the aircraft to stall; it entered an uncontrolled nose dive and crashed into a paddy field at 06:55. The accident killed 44 of 53 occupants. The investigation found that the crew did not use the weather radar on board and were unaware of a second storm cell in the approach.
probable_cause: The crew failed to utilize the aircraft's weather radar and received no information of severe weather in the approach due to no change in the ATIS Special Weather Report. The pilots believed ATC would not direct them into a storm. The aircraft encountered a thunderstorm and downdraft that caused an aerodynamic stall at low altitude from which recovery was impossible.

factors.evidence: Aircraft entered a severe thunderstorm during approach; sudden downdraft struck the plane at 1,500 feet causing the nose to go up and the plane to stall
Downdraft caused nose to pitch up and the plane to stall
Aircraft entered nose dive 30 seconds after stall and could not recover before impact
Aircraft crashed into paddy field at 6:55am, skidded 510 feet before breaking up
Severe thunderstorm conditions restricted visibility during approach and recovery attempt
The weather radar on board was not used
Pilots did not realize that there was a second storm in the approach beyond the one they observed

events.text: Flight 231 departed Khon Kaen at 05:50 local time bound for Don Mueang Airport
Aircraft began descent from cruise altitude toward Don Mueang
Entered severe thunderstorm during approach to runway 21R
Sudden downdraft struck the aircraft at 1,500 feet, causing nose to pitch up
Aircraft stalled in response to downdraft
Nose dive began 30 seconds after stall onset as aircraft lost lift
Banked slightly to the right and crashed into paddy field, skidding 510 feet and breaking up; fire started but was extinguished by heavy rain

notes: Investigation provided possible causes rather than formal probable cause
Precise times for some events inferred from narrative

title: Itavia 870
summary: Itavia Flight 870 departed Bologna at 20:08 CEST on 27 June 1980 for a scheduled service to Palermo with 77 passengers and 4 crew members. Contact was lost at 20:37 after the aircraft reported its position over the Tyrrhenian Sea near Ustica, about 120 km southwest of Naples. At 20:59 CEST, the aircraft broke apart in mid-air and crashed with no survivors. The technical commission concluded a bomb hidden in the rear lavatory caused destruction, but the Parliamentary Commission on Terrorism suggested alternative hypotheses of missile attack or international military action. A Palermo civil tribunal ruled the Italian government failed to protect the flight, concealing truth and destroying evidence.
probable_cause: The cause remains officially disputed. The technical commission concluded a bomb hidden in the rear lavatory caused the aircraft's destruction. The Parliamentary Commission on Terrorism identified the crash as possibly part of an act of war or military action. Italian government has faced legal judgments for failing to protect the flight and concealing evidence.

factors.evidence: a Palermo civil tribunal ordered the Italian government to pay 100 million euros for failing to protect the flight, concealing the truth and destroying evidence

technical commission concluded that a bomb hidden in the rear lavatory caused the aircraft's destruction; Prime Minister attributed crash to shooting down by a French missile during dogfight between Libyan and French fighter jets
aircraft was vulnerable to destruction from bomb or missile attack without adequate structural protection or detection
the aircraft broke apart in mid-air and crashed

events.text: On 27 June 1980 at 20:08 CEST, the aircraft departed with a delay of one hour and 53 minutes from Bologna Guglielmo Marconi Airport for a scheduled service to Palermo
Contact was lost shortly after the last message from the aircraft was received at 20:37, giving its position over the Tyrrhenian Sea near the island of Ustica, about 120 km southwest of Naples
At 20:59 CEST, the aircraft broke apart in mid-air and crashed
Two Italian Air Force F-104s were scrambled at 21:00 from Grosseto Air Force Base to locate the crash area and search for any survivors but failed to locate the area because of poor visibility

notes: Cause remains disputed and highly contested; technical commission conclusion of bomb not universally accepted
Italian government has faced legal judgments for concealing evidence
Case officially closed in 2007 but remains controversial

title: Aeroflot 4225
summary: Aeroflot Flight 4225 took off from Alma-Ata at 00:39 in a heat wave with the aircraft at maximum takeoff weight. Only a few seconds after takeoff at 500 ft, the flight encountered a zone of hot air and was caught in a downdraft. The Tupolev stalled and plummeted nose down into a farm near Alma-Ata suburbs, slid into a ravine, caught fire and disintegrated, killing all 166 people on board. Investigation concluded the crash was caused by windshear while aircraft was near maximum takeoff weight.
probable_cause: Windshear and downdraft during initial climb when aircraft was at or near maximum takeoff weight for ambient conditions.

factors.evidence: The Tupolev stalled and plummeted nose down
crash was caused by windshear which took place while the aircraft was near its maximum takeoff weight
aircraft stalled and plummeted nose down into a farm

events.text: Flight 4225 took off from Alma-Ata Airport at 00:39 local time in a heat wave.
Only a few seconds after takeoff, the flight reached 500 ft when the plane reached a zone of hot air.
The Tupolev was caught in a downdraft.
The aircraft stalled and plummeted nose down into a farm near the suburbs of Alma-Ata.
The aircraft slid into a ravine, caught fire and disintegrated, killing everyone on board.

title: Saudia 163
summary: Saudia Flight 163, a Lockheed L-1011 TriStar flying Karachi to Jeddah via Riyadh, suffered a cargo-compartment fire seven minutes after departing Riyadh on 19 August 1980. The flight deck crew, all newly qualified on the TriStar, spent several minutes confirming the smoke warnings before Captain Khowyter made a successful emergency landing back at Riyadh. After the aircraft stopped, rescue crews found the wing engines still running and could not open the doors; with no evacuation carried out, all 301 aboard died of smoke inhalation.
probable_cause: Investigators could not determine the source of the cargo compartment fire and were unable to establish why the crew, despite a successful emergency landing, never evacuated the aircraft before all aboard died of smoke inhalation.

factors.evidence: Almost seven minutes into the flight the crew received warnings of smoke from the cargo compartment.
All three flight deck crew were inexperienced on the TriStar; the first officer received his type rating just 11 days before the accident.
The crew spent the next four minutes trying to confirm the warnings before Flight Engineer Curtis went into the cabin to check.
Captain Khowyter declared an emergency and landed back at Riyadh, using the entire length of the runway to stop.
Rescue personnel found the wing-mounted engines still running, preventing them from opening the doors; all died of smoke inhalation.

events.text: Flight 163 took off from Riyadh at 21:08 bound for Jeddah after a two-hour refueling layover.
Almost seven minutes into the flight the crew received warnings of smoke from the aft cargo compartment.
The crew spent four minutes trying to confirm the warnings before Flight Engineer Curtis went into the cabin and confirmed smoke.
Captain Khowyter decided to return to the airport, and First Officer Hasanain radioed their intentions at 21:20.
At 21:25 the number two engine's thrust lever jammed as the fire burned through its operating cable; it was shut down on final approach.
After the aircraft stopped at 21:39, rescue crews found the wing engines still running and could not open the doors; no evacuation occurred.

notes: Investigating agency not named in source text
Fire's ignition source and reason for failed evacuation were never determined per the article
